summary: pp.1-12: Pages 1 through 12 of IESO's Technical Requirements for Large Computational Loads Connecting to the Ontario Power System (Version 1.0) covering purpose, applicability, interconnection process, project data requirements, and technical interconnection limits including single-point-failure load loss, periodic oscillation, load ramping, power factor, damping, ride-through capabilities, and UFLS. | pp.13-21: Pages 13 through 21 of the IESO Technical Requirements for Large Computational Loads cover UFLS relay settings, phasor measurement, dynamic disturbance recording, voltage/short-circuit/protection/telemetry/metering/commissioning obligations, and Appendix A detailed system assessment criteria (thermal, voltage, stability, interface, relay margin, small-signal, load fluctuation, EMT, and resource adequacy).

constraints.snippet: No internal single point failure within the project results in a load loss above 600 MW or a lower value identified by system assessments.
constraints.notes: Maximum permissible load loss from any internal single point failure; a lower value may be specified by system assessments.

constraints.snippet: Automatic load transfer between different supplies from system to the project is not acceptable.
constraints.notes: Prohibits automatic load transfer between different system supplies.

constraints.snippet: In accordance with Appendix 4.3 of the Market Rules, the connection applicant shall ensure the project has the capability to maintain the power factor within the range of 0.9 lagging and 0.9 leading as measured at the defined meter point of the project.
constraints.notes: Power factor capability requirement between 0.9 lagging and 0.9 leading at the defined meter point.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure the project does not introduce any net negative damping to system oscillations within the sub-synchronous frequency range.
constraints.notes: Qualitative prohibition against net negative damping in the sub-synchronous frequency range.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure the power consumption at the Point of Interconnection (POI) of the project has no periodic power oscillation within the sub-synchronous frequency band exceeding the lesser of +/-2.5 MW or +/-0.25 % of the nominal power of the project unless the connection applicant provides the specific load profile which will be assessed by the IESO.
constraints.notes: Absolute (+/-2.5 MW) half of the lesser-of periodic power oscillation limit at the POI within the sub-synchronous frequency band to avoid SSTI/SSCI. [CONFLICT: Conflicts with fluctuation_band_5 (p.8: 0.25 % of rated load = 0.25 MW)]

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure the power consumption at the Point of Interconnection (POI) of the project has no periodic power oscillation within the sub-synchronous frequency band exceeding the lesser of +/-2.5 MW or +/-0.25 % of the nominal power of the project unless the connection applicant provides the specific load profile which will be assessed by the IESO.
constraints.notes: Percentage (+/-0.25% of nominal power) half of the lesser-of periodic power oscillation limit at the POI within the sub-synchronous frequency band to avoid SSTI/SSCI. [CONFLICT: Conflicts with fluctuation_band_4 (p.8: 2.5 MW = 2.5 MW)]

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure that the load fluctuation frequency at the project does not exceed the limit specified in Ref 5, Appendix 2 of Transmission System Code, based on the voltage fluctuation magnitude caused by the project.
constraints.notes: References external Transmission System Code Appendix 2 limits based on voltage fluctuation magnitude.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure that the project has the capability to operate with linear ramp rates not exceeding 20 MW per minute during normal operation. This maximum rate applies when reducing active power consumption and when restoring active power consumption, unless a different ramp rate has been specified by the IESO.
constraints.notes: Applies to normal operation when reducing or restoring active power; does not restrict response during system events such as RAS runbacks or frequency/voltage excursions.

constraints.snippet: In accordance with Appendix 4.3 of the Market Rules, the connection applicant shall ensure the project has the capability to ride-through routine switching events and design criteria contingencies on the transmission system assuming standard fault detection, auxiliary relaying, communication, and rated breaker interrupting times, unless disconnection by configuration or a lower-level ride-through capability has been approved by the IESO.
constraints.notes: General ride-through capability requirement for switching events and design criteria contingencies.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure that the project has the capability to ride-through voltage disturbances of the magnitude and duration specified in Table 1 and Figure 1 at the Point of Interconnection (POI). The project shall have the capability to ride-through two consecutive voltage disturbances in Table 1 occurring within a 30 s interval.
constraints.notes: Voltage ride-through table: <=1.2 Vmax and >1.05 Vmax for 2 s; <=1.05 Vmax and >Vmax for 1800 s; <=Vmax and >=Vmin continuous; <Vmin and >=0.8 Vnom for 2 s; <0.8 Vnom and >=0.5 Vnom for 0.5 s; <0.5 Vnom and >=0.2 Vnom for 0.25 s; <0.2 Vnom for 0.16 s.

constraints.snippet: During a system disturbance causing voltage depression, the load supplied by the UPSs at the project shall only reduce active power consumption proportional to voltage sag for the POI voltage between 0.5 and 0.8 pu and may cease to withdraw power from the system only when the POI voltage goes below 0.5 pu. Switching to UPS supply while ceasing to withdraw power from the system is not allowed for voltage rise at the POI, for voltages up to 5% above the maximum continuous voltage (corresponding to physical voltages 578 kV, 263 kV, 133 kV for voltage levels 500 kV, 230 kV and 115 kV, respectively).
constraints.notes: UPS active power behavior during voltage depressions and prohibition on UPS transfer during voltage rises up to 1.05 Vmax.

constraints.snippet: After the system disturbance is cleared and the POI voltage recovers within the ORTAC post-contingency voltage range, the project shall restore its active power withdrawal from the system to the level that exists prior to the system disturbance within a restoration time that is set to 1 second by default and configurable by the IESO based on system assessments. No ramp rate limitations shall be applied to restrict the project's response rate to recover its active power.
constraints.notes: Post-fault active power recovery time requirement (1 s default, configurable by IESO); ramp rate limits do not apply to recovery.

constraints.snippet: During and following the system disturbance, the project shall not be switched to the backup generation supply unless the disturbance trips the project by configuration. If the project has been switched to the backup generation supply, it shall not be reconnected automatically without the IESO's approval.
constraints.notes: Prohibits switching to backup generation during disturbances unless tripped by configuration, and prohibits automatic reconnection.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure that the project has the capability to ride-through frequency disturbance of the magnitude and duration specified in Table 2 and Figure 2. During the frequency disturbance, the project shall maintain its active power consumption at the level prior to the disturbance. The use of UPS is not allowed during the ride-through period.
constraints.notes: Frequency ride-through table: >61.8 Hz may trip; >61.2 Hz for 299 s; <=61.2 and >=58.8 Hz continuous; <58.8 Hz for 10 s; <57 Hz for 0 s.

constraints.snippet: Within the frequency ride-through range per Table 2, the connection applicant shall ensure the project has the capability to ride-through frequency excursions having an absolute RoCoF magnitude that is less than or equal to 5.0 Hz/s. RoCoF shall be calculated as the average RoCoF over a rolling 0.5 second averaging window.
constraints.source_section: 6.7.3 Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) Ride-Through
constraints.notes: Must maintain pre-disturbance active power without UPS during RoCoF excursions up to 5.0 Hz/s over a 0.5 s rolling window.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure the project has the capability to ride-through positive-sequence phase angle jump initiated by no-fault switching events within a sub-cycle time frame of the POI voltage of less than or equal to 25 electrical degrees.
constraints.notes: Must maintain pre-disturbance active power without UPS during sub-cycle phase angle jumps up to 25 electrical degrees.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure the project has the capability to ride-through grid disturbances with V/Hz, measured at the POI, of at least 1.1 per unit for 45 seconds, 1.18 per unit for 2 seconds, and 1.27 per unit for 1 second.
constraints.notes: Must maintain pre-disturbance active power without UPS during V/Hz disturbances up to 1.1 pu (45 s), 1.18 pu (2 s), and 1.27 pu (1 s).

constraints.snippet: According to Section 10.4.6 of Chapter 5 of the Market Rules and Section 11.3 of the Market Manual 7.1, the connection applicant is required to participate in the UFLS program if it has a total peak load greater than 25 MW at all its owned facilities. The connection applicant must select 35% of total peak
constraints.notes: UFLS participation obligation for facilities with total peak load > 25 MW; sentence continues onto page 13.

constraints.snippet: However, the connection applicant shall provide the provision and capability to select all UPS-supplied loads in the project for under-frequency tripping, potentially at different tripping thresholds than the current UFLS settings, which may be required by the IESO in the future as the system evolves.
constraints.notes: Requires capability to enroll all UPS-supplied loads in under-frequency load shedding.

constraints.snippet: To comply with the short tripping time in the UFLS program, the IT load can be switched to UPS supply firstly, then switched to backup generation supply. They shall not be reconnected back to the system automatically without the IESO's approval.
constraints.notes: Prohibits automatic reconnection of UFLS-tripped IT loads without IESO approval.

constraints.snippet: Table 3 summarizes UFLS relay settings as a function of the total peak load of all facilities owned by the connection applicant.
constraints.notes: Specifies UFLS frequency thresholds (59.5 to 58.9 Hz), operating times (0.3 s; 10.0 s anti-stall), and cumulative load shed percentages (35% to 37%) by aggregate summer peak load tier (>=25 MW, >=50 MW, >=100 MW).

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant, in conjunction with the transmitter, must also ensure that capacitor banks connected to the same station bus as the load are shed by UFLS facilities at 59.5 Hz with a time delay of 3 seconds.
constraints.notes: Under-frequency shedding requirement for station bus capacitor banks at 59.5 Hz with a 3-second delay.

constraints.snippet: The maximum load that can be connected to any single UFLS relay is 150 MW to ensure that the inadvertent operation of a single under-frequency relay during the transient period following a system disturbance does not lead to further system instability.
constraints.notes: Protection design limit restricting maximum load per single UFLS relay to 150 MW.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant is required to install permanent equipment and infrastructure required for phasor measurement and to provide synchrophasor data that comply with Market Manual 1.7.
constraints.notes: Applies to transmission-connected projects with MVA rating >= 20 MVA.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant is required to install a permanent device for dynamic disturbance recording that meets the technical specifications provided in Section 2.7 of Market Manual 1.6.
constraints.notes: Applies to transmission-connected projects with MVA rating >= 20 MVA.

constraints.snippet: The project's equipment shall meet the voltage requirements specified in Section 2.4.2 and Section 2.4.3 of the ORTAC.
constraints.notes: General requirement for all load facilities.

constraints.snippet: According to Section 6.1.2 of the TSC, the project's transmission connection equipment shall be designed to withstand the fault levels in the area.
constraints.notes: Equipment and circuit breakers must withstand and interrupt local fault levels per TSC Appendix 2 and ORTAC Sections 2.4.2 and 2.4.3.

constraints.snippet: Associated overvoltage protective relaying must be set to ensure that the project's equipment does not automatically trip for voltages up to 5% above the equipment's corresponding maximum continuous voltage as specified in section 4.2 of the ORTAC.
constraints.notes: Overvoltage relay non-tripping margin of 5% above maximum continuous voltage.

constraints.snippet: BPS elements are deemed by the IESO to be essential to system reliability and security and must be protected by redundant protection systems in accordance with Section 8.2 of the TSC.
constraints.notes: Redundant, physically separated protection also required for transmission voltage BES elements rated above 100 kV.

constraints.snippet: According to Section 7.5 of Chapter 4 of the Market Rules, the connection applicant shall provide to the IESO the applicable telemetry data listed in Appendix 4.17 of the Market Rules on a continual basis for transmission connected projects, or in Appendix 4.18 of the Market Rules for distribution connected projects.
constraints.notes: Continual telemetry and monitoring equipment compliance per Market Rules.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall ensure the wholesale metering installations comply with (i) the Ontario Market Rules, e.g., Chapter 6 - Wholesale Metering, Chapter 6 - Appendices, Chapter 9 - Settlements and Billing, Chapter 9 - Appendices, Chapter 10-Transmssion Service and Planning, (ii) the applicable market manuals, e.g., Market Manual 3 Series: Metering, and (iii) IESO wholesale metering hardware standards and policies.
constraints.notes: Wholesale metering compliance obligation.

constraints.snippet: The connection applicant shall submit generic composite load model and User Defined Models (UDMs) for both PSS/E (Version 36 or later) and DSA (Version 22 or later). The connection applicant shall also submit a final PSCAD model as well as a study report that benchmarks the generic composite load model and UDM against the EMT model to ensure that the model performance is consistent across different simulation platforms.
constraints.source_section: IESO - Section 6.16 Commissioning Tests and Performance Validation
constraints.notes: Requires as-built simulation models, benchmarking, and type or on-site commissioning test validation.

constraints.snippet: If upgrades are needed, the IESO may direct the transmitter or the distributor to disconnect the project until such upgrades are deployed, to the satisfaction of the IESO. Automatic reconnection of the facilities to the system is not allowed.
constraints.source_section: IESO - Section 6.17 Failure to Meet IESO's Requirements
constraints.notes: Non-compliance disconnection and prohibition on automatic reconnection.

constraints.snippet: Each capacitor bank shall be sized to ensure that voltage declines or rises at delivery point buses on switching operations will not exceed 4% of steady state rms voltage before tap changer action.
constraints.source_section: IESO - Appendix A.2 Steady-State Voltage Assessment
constraints.notes: Maximum 4% steady-state rms voltage change during capacitor bank switching before tap changer action.

constraints.snippet: After the fault is cleared, the load shall be switched to the system supply as fast as possible. Further generation rejection may be employed if needed. When generation rejection is employed, the same amount of load at the project shall also be switched to its backup generation supply and not reconnected to the system without the IESO's approval.
constraints.notes: Post-fault UPS return and generation-rejection load switching requirements for projects in generation areas.

constraints.snippet: According to Section 2.4.1 of ORTAC, the project shall not be permitted to lower power transfer capability or operating security limits by 5% or more.
constraints.notes: Maximum permitted reduction in system power transfer capability or operating security limits.

constraints.snippet: According to the Market Rules for the line distance protection, following fault clearing, the margin on all instantaneous and timed distance relays at stations that are part of the BES and BPS must be at least 20% and 10% respectively.
constraints.notes: Minimum line distance protection relay margins of 20% (instantaneous) and 10% (timed) at BES/BPS stations.

constraints.snippet: As per Section 6.3 in this document, the connection applicant shall ensure the project does not introduce any net negative damping to system oscillations.
constraints.source_section: IESO - Appendix A.6 Small-Signal Stability Assessment
constraints.notes: Qualitative small-signal stability damping requirement.

constraints.snippet: Based on the overall adverse impact, a corrective action such as Grid Forming (GFM) batteries and E-STATCOMs may be required to mitigate the impact of the project's load fluctuations.
constraints.source_section: IESO - Appendix A.7 Load Fluctuation Assessment
constraints.notes: Qualitative mitigation requirement following SIA load fluctuation assessment (voltage, interface margin, intertie phase shifter duty, and AGC impact).

constraints.snippet: After the IESO has confirmed the EMT model is acceptable, the connection applicant shall use the accepted EMT model to benchmark UDM and composite model for the project and submit both models to the IESO.
constraints.notes: EMT model benchmarking requirement for UDM and composite models.

constraints.snippet: Alternatively, the connection applicant is required to agree to curtail all or part of their load when necessary to maintain system balance.
constraints.source_section: IESO - Appendix A.9 Global Resource Adequacy Assessment
constraints.notes: Applies if the project is too large and causes global resource inadequacy.
